data.creative: Kid swears off freezing, shows bottle, warts nearly gone · 996534642081945
data.hook: I'm never freezing my son's warts again.
data.desire: Get rid of my kid's warts without the freezing that hurts, so he stops hiding his finger at school.
data.angle: Failed effort: doctor freezing and store remedies did not work, a mom-bought bottle did.
data.belief_shift: from 'warts need painful freezing at the doctor' → to 'a gentle drop at home can work, even for a kid'
data.script_structure: Freezing-clinic hook with mom inset → kid names the problem (2 years) → list of failed fixes (doctor freezing, store remedies) → mom got me this (bottle reveal) → routine (2x a day, a month) → result + school confidence → 'worked like magic' endorsement from other moms → CTA 'go get yours today'
data.mechanism_reveal: NO EVIDENCE: no mechanism; only usage routine (twice a day for about a month).
data.proof: Kid testimonial with claimed result (warts 'almost all the way gone'), finger shown to camera at 0:23, add-on clips of other mom-and-kid pairs endorsing it.
data.cta: So go get yours today! (button: Shop Now). No offer stated in video.
data.why_it_works: Interpretation of execution, not measured performance: The hook turns a feared treatment (freezing a child's wart) into a vow, which every parent who has sat through it understands. A real kid speaking plainly about hiding his finger at school makes the stake social, not medical. The bottle enters only after the failed-fixes list, so it lands as the answer.
data.transferable_move: Open on the painful old fix as a vow ('I'm never doing X again'), list what failed in the user's own words, then reveal the product as the thing a parent brought home. Soften: talk about hiding a hand and rough skin, not 'warts gone'.
data.opening_visual: Gloved clinician freezing a wart on a child's foot with a cryo canister, circular inset of a smiling girl holding the amber bottle, text 'I'm NEVER freezing my son's warts again!'
data.transition_to_product: 0:11.6–14.6 'nothing has worked until my mom got me this' — boy pushes the bottle at the camera at 0:14.
data.proof_placement: Result claim follows the routine beat (0:18–22); finger shown at 0:23; other-family endorsement clips follow the result (0:24–28).
